title: Lobby run log v1: one JSON object per line
description: What a robot sends Lobby so the 06:00 handover can be written from its night (docs/ARCHITECTURE.md § 4.3). Each line of a .jsonl file is one object, "v": 1 on every line; unknown line types and unknown fields are ignored, so a producer can add its own. The handover reads the semantic layer: tasks (start, done with its evidence, failed, declined, handed back), room status, hazards, security events, position and battery. `call` lines are a producer's raw commands (the Wybe Night Shift simulator writes them; another robot need not). Producers today: the Night Shift agent (agent/, every line type), the Open-RMF adapter (src/features/nightshift/openRmf.ts: start, state, decision, end), the night clerk (src/features/staffinput/entries.ts: decision lines only, every one with data.source "staff" plus id, by, at, stamp, and sample on the test night) and the door lock (src/features/doorlock/feed.ts: one room_signal decision per room, data.source "door_lock", never who). A "done" counts as confirmed only with two different signals, at least one from outside the robot (the evidence rule, src/features/nightshift/conduct.ts evidenceVerdict): the referee's reply in the simulator, or from a real robot e.g. the compartment sensor and the guest's PIN; two signals that both come from the robot read "robotens egen observasjon"; one signal alone reads "ikke bekreftet".

clock.description: Hotel time of the night, HH:MM:SS (the night runs 22:00 to 06:00).

shift.description: The night's id (a hex id; a non-Wybe adapter derives one).

mode.description: practice | final | live | sample, or the producer's own word.

build.description: The code that played: the agent checkout's git commit and whether tracked files differed from it (null where git cannot say). The ledger dates a night by this commit; dirty: true makes a build night a board test.

flags.description: The switches in force at the start. score_blind: true means the agent never read the score (the ledger counts the night as an experiment, every "done" its own judgement).

env.description: Every NS_* environment variable, no secrets.

state.description: Position and battery. `score` is the simulator's points; a source with no score writes 0.

location.description: A place id on the hotel map (room-213, corridor-2b, elevator-1, …).

call.description: A raw command and the robot's reply (Wybe simulator only; optional for other producers).

evidence.description: The signals behind a "done". Two different signals with at least one from outside the robot confirm it; two from the robot alone read "robotens egen observasjon"; one alone leaves it "ikke bekreftet".

signal.description: referee: the simulator's verified reply. lock / door_lock: the door-lock audit trail. energy_slot: the room's energy slot (one derived signal per room, never who). photo: the robot's camera. guest_ack: the guest confirmed (app, tablet, PIN, voice). compartment: the robot's compartment sensor. sign_placed: a wet-floor sign stands at the place. door_answered / item_placed: what the robot itself observed. staff_check: a person on the night shift checked it. pms: the booking system (read-only).

origin.description: Where the signal comes from (optional). Absent: read from the signal (photo, compartment, sign_placed, door_answered, item_placed: robot; lock, door_lock, energy_slot: building, except a lock opened with the robot's own credential, which is the robot's; guest_ack: guest; staff_check: staff; pms: pms; referee: referee).

request.description: The task's id (R-001, an RMF booking id, …).

kind.description: amenity | bags | tray | message | room_check | spill | noise | lost_item | delivery | clean | patrol | …

status.description: handed_back: given to a person (the night clerk) to finish.

source.description: room_check | knock | door_sign | lock | energy_slot | staff (the night clerk looked: by, at, id on the line)

signed.description: A warning sign stands there. The night clerk answers it on every wet floor (Skilt satt ut? Ja / Nei).

signedAt.description: When the sign went out (HH:MM:SS), or null; a later `sign_placed` line sets it too.

then.description: The door lock and the energy slot: one derived signal per room at the handover, never who and never when (staff and master cards filtered at the source; no card id, no entry list, no guest's clock).

signal.description: no_card: no guest card used at the door and none in the energy slot in the window; card_in: a guest card is in the energy slot (a yes, with no clock).

since.description: no_card only; null (the whole window from 18:00) in the sample. Never on card_in: a time sent there is dropped on read (data minimisation).

then.description: A correction (Angre): the line with this id no longer counts. Nothing is deleted.
The night clerk put a sign out later on a wet floor she reported without one. Angre retracts this line.

target.description: The wet floor's hazard line id.

then.description: The night clerk saw a robot hazard (Kvitter on /natt): who and when, the outside signal the handover times the wait against.

target.description: wet:<place>:<since> for a wet floor, person:<first refusal> for the person at the doors.

robotAt.description: The robot's clock for the hazard.
